q: What are the six stops of a query, in order?
options: Connect, parse, plan, run, memory, disk
Parse, connect, run, plan, disk, memory
Plan, parse, connect, memory, run, disk
Connect, plan, parse, disk, memory, run

q: You misspell a column name. Where does the query fail?
options: In the executor, after reading all rows
In the parser, before any row is read
On disk
At COMMIT
why: Typos and unknown names fail early. Bad math, like dividing by zero, fails late.

q: What is the planner's cost number?
options: The exact time in milliseconds
The size of the result
A score for comparing ways to run the query. It is a guess, not a time
The memory used
why: Wrong notes make a wrong plan. After a big load, run ANALYZE.

q: In EXPLAIN (BUFFERS) output, what does `shared hit` mean?
options: The page was read from disk
The page was written to the log
The page was locked
The page was found in memory, with no disk read
why: hit is memory, read is not. A page is always 8 KB.

q: For a write, what happens first, and what does COMMIT wait for?
options: The log is written first, and COMMIT waits for the log to be safe on disk. The table can be written later
The table is written first, then the log
Both are written at the same time with no waiting
Only the table, the log is optional

q: What does an UPDATE do to the row on disk?
options: Changes the bytes in place
Writes a new row and leaves a dead old row, so the row moves
Deletes the old row at once and frees the space
Writes only the changed column
why: This is why dead rows and VACUUM exist (lesson 16).
